CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, native-code, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zupmxode simulates population PK/PD models, written in a subset of the rxode2 model language, over NONMEM-style event records, in parallel over subjects, with no C compiler on the machine. Models are parsed in R, compiled to the package’s own IR, and turned into native code (or run in MIR’s interpreter) through zumir. It is a simulation engine with a C API for estimators; it is not an estimator, not a new model language, and has no Imports.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0047. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides. The whole package rests on D2 (MIR through zumir), which is provisional on zumir’s Stage 0 spike; §11.1 of the design says what changes if the spike fails.

Current state

Stage 0 (package identity and CI) done 2026-11-15; no engine functionality yet. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 for v0.1.0. Siblings that will depend on it: zupmxfit (RFC 0072, through zupmxode_subject_eval()) and zupmxio (RFC 0046, Suggests both ways). It will link to zumir and zuexact; zumir is not on CRAN yet, so it comes through Remotes: until it is, and its release gates this package’s submission.

Commands

  • make -C tests/c check: the C core built and tested without R’s headers. Part of the default loop once a stage touches src/core/.
  • bash tools/ci/platform.sh <os>: every per-OS check, as CI runs it.
  • Rscript tools/make-corpus.R: regenerates the oracle fixtures (about 2 minutes; needs rxode2, mrgsolve and nlmixr2lib). Occasional: when the corpus or an oracle changes.
  • tools/run-benchmarks [engine]: the §10 rows, appended to .agents/benchmarks.csv; run alone on an idle machine.

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md §4. The engine is C in src/core/, which never includes R’s headers, so the C tests, fuzz harnesses and mutation runs build it alone; src/zupmxode.c is the only R glue and registers the .Call entry points.

Invariants that are easy to break

These are fixed by the design before any code exists; each names the section that decides it.

  • No Imports, ever (§2, §12). A runtime dependency breaks the “stock R installation” promise the package exists for.
  • C code never calls error() and never touches an R object inside the parallel region or zupmxode_subject_eval(); it returns status codes and writes into caller-owned buffers (§4.4, §4.6, §8). Breaking it makes the engine unsafe for estimators calling it from threads.
  • Random draws happen only in R, with R’s RNG (D7). C is deterministic, so results are reproducible from set.seed() at any thread count.
  • MIR is reached only through zumir’s C API and never vendored here (D14); the IR is the package’s own and nothing outside the lowering depends on MIR (D13).
  • The two tiers must give identical doubles, and output must be bitwise identical across thread counts (§6.3, §9). A difference is a bug unless traced to a recorded contraction.

Testing

Conformance suite: the oracle fixtures in tests/testthat/fixtures/oracle/, written by tools/make-corpus.R (design §7 says how). Regenerate them, never edit them; a new disagreements.csv row needs its note in disagreements.md, or test-oracle-fixtures.R fails.

Helpers:

  • helper-tables.R: expect_table_equal() at the §6.3 tolerances, through dazdiff when installed; table_differences() is the local route, tested on its own.
  • helper-oracle.R: reads fixtures and solves with rxode2. The generator sources it, so tests and fixtures solve the same way.

The suite runs shuffled, top-level code included: build test data inside test_that() or in a helper, never at file level. Runtime: about 20 s locally, most of it rxode2 compiling three models.

Continuous integration

Shared r-actions workflows, called from .github/workflows/: R-CMD-check.yaml (with the Windows R-devel row), native-checks.yaml (valgrind, LTO, rchk, analyzers, cran-special; sanitizers from Stage 2, r-actions#68), gctorture.yaml (wide step on pull requests, step 20 daily and on dispatch), coverage.yaml (native: true), assurance.yaml and platforms.yaml. pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site.

platforms.yaml runs tools/ci/platform.sh: today the C core built and tested without R (make -C tests/c), Ubuntu only until Stage 2 adds macOS and Windows. Dispatch step-20 gctorture on the branch (gh workflow run gctorture.yml --ref <branch>) before merging a change to PROTECTs, finalizers or external pointers. The roadmap’s full stages are 2, 6, 8 and the three closing ones.

Vendored native code

liblsoda (sdwfrost/liblsoda, MIT), made re-entrant per thread (D5). Not vendored yet: record the pinned commit and every local patch here when it is.
